kf: **Mycosis fungoides (MF)** is the commonest cutaneous T-cell lymphoma: slowly evolving patches, plaques and sometimes tumours.
Patches in **sun-protected 'bathing trunk'** areas (buttocks, hips, breasts), varying shape, mild itch; often misdiagnosed as eczema or psoriasis for years.
Repeated biopsies (off steroids) with T-cell receptor gene studies may be needed.
Early stage: skin-directed therapy (potent steroids, phototherapy, radiotherapy); most have a normal life expectancy.
**Sézary syndrome**: erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, circulating malignant T cells: specialist.

sub: Adults 50–70; men twice as often; about 0.5 per 100,000 per year.

myths: **"Lymphoma always spreads quickly"**: early MF is indolent; most never progress.
patho_lead: MF is a **clonal expansion of skin-homing CD4+ T cells** that infiltrate the epidermis.

mech.t: A clone of memory CD4+ T cells carries skin-homing receptors (CLA, CCR4).
Malignant cells invade the epidermis, forming Pautrier microabscesses.
Over years, deeper infiltration produces plaques and tumours.
mech.cap: Mycosis fungoides evolves from patch to plaque to tumour.

mech.t: Rarely, cells reach nodes and blood (advanced stage, Sézary).

histo: Atypical cerebriform lymphocytes in the epidermis (epidermotropism), Pautrier microabscesses; CD4+, loss of CD7; clonal TCR rearrangement.
prog: Stage IA: normal life expectancy; advanced stages much poorer.
